candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'And his body was white as snow and red as the blooming of a rose, and the hair of his head and his long locks were white as wool, and his eyes beautiful. And when he opened his eyes, he lighted up the whole house like the sun, and the whole house was very bright' — the miraculous birth of Noah. Tewahedo iconography preserves the radiant-infant motif (the depiction of saints' birth-narratives in some monastic frescoes shows infant-light radiating from the cradle) — drawing on the Enochic Noah-birth as one of its scriptural-iconographic anchors.

1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'And his father Lamech was afraid of him, and fled and came to his own father Methuselah. And he said to him: I have begotten a strange son, diverse from and unlike man, and resembling the sons of the God of heaven; and his nature is different and he is not like us' — Lamech's anxiety about Noah's supernatural appearance. Tewahedo theological tradition preserves the distinction between APPEARING supernatural and BEING supernaturally fathered: Noah is righteous-Adamic, not Watcher-fathered — the Epistle is careful to refute the latter possibility through the rest of the chapter.

candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'And call his name Noah, for he shall be left to you, and he and his sons will be saved from the destruction, which is coming upon the earth on account of all the sin and all the unrighteousness, which will be consummated on the earth in his days' — the prophecy of the Flood delivered through Methuselah-Lamech-Noah lineage. Tewahedo Flood-theology preserves the prophetic-foreknowledge component: the Flood was ANNOUNCED in advance through the patriarchal line, giving humanity warning and time to repent — emphasising God's mercy even in judgment.
